procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Delhi at New Delhi
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 20.07.2017 of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in Writ Petition (C) Nos. 12313 of 2015, 602 of 2017 and CM No. 2775 of 2017.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court allowed the writ petitions and issued directions.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's judgment and order, restored the Writ Petitions and C.M. to the High Court's file, and directed the High Court to reconsider all aspects of the matter afresh on its own merits and in accordance with law (de novo), uninfluenced by any observations made in the original High Court judgment. The Supreme Court explicitly stated that it was not expressing any opinion on the issues to be adjudicated by the High Court.

issue.issue_text: Whether the impugned judgment should be set aside and the matter relegated to the High Court for fresh consideration on all aspects.

facts: The case came to the Supreme Court as an appeal against a High Court judgment.
The High Court had directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to conduct an investigation.
The appellants argued that the High Court's decision was flawed because it had misdirected itself.
Specifically, the appellants contended that the High Court had mistaken the initial allegations in a CBI Preliminary Enquiry (PE) for the final conclusions of that enquiry.

The appellants asserted that the CBI's actual prima facie opinion, after the PE, was that it was not a fit case for CBI investigation as there was no involvement of public servants or loss to public funds, and that the State police could handle it.
application: The Supreme Court observed that the appeal involved several "contentious issues" that had not been properly examined.
Instead of examining these complex issues for the first time at the Supreme Court level, the Court decided it was more appropriate to send the case back to the High Court.
The Court's rationale was to allow the High Court to conduct a fresh and complete reconsideration of all aspects of the matter.

To ensure a fair and unbiased new hearing, the Supreme Court explicitly stated that it was not expressing any opinion on the merits of the issues and that the High Court should not be influenced by the previous, now-overturned, judgment.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court allowed the appeals, set aside the impugned High Court judgment, and relegated (sent back) the matter to the High Court for a fresh decision on its own merits and in accordance with the law.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the impugned judgment should be set aside and the matter relegated to the High Court for fresh consideration on all aspects.
appellant_arguments: The appellant's arguments are not explicitly stated in the text. However, it can be inferred from the court's decision that the appellant raised several "contentious issues" and argued that the Supreme Court should not examine them for the first time, but instead, the matter should be sent back to the High Court for fresh consideration.
respondent_arguments: The arguments for the respondent are not mentioned in the provided text.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: When an appellate court finds it more appropriate for a lower court to consider contentious issues for the first time, it may set aside the lower court's judgment and remand the matter for a fresh hearing on its merits.
obiter: The court explicitly expressed no opinion on the merits of the issues that require adjudication by the lower court upon remand.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Supreme Court found it inappropriate to be the first forum to examine the various "contentious issues" raised in the appeals. Instead of adjudicating these complex matters itself, the Court concluded that the proper judicial course was to set aside the High Court's judgment and remand the case for a fresh, comprehensive consideration of all aspects by the High Court.
legal_tests_applied: The court did not apply a specific legal test but acted on the procedural principle of judicial propriety, which dictates that an appellate court should not typically decide complex or contentious issues for the first time on appeal, but should instead remand the matter to the lower court for a full initial consideration.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant was successful in this appeal.
why_respondent_won: The respondent was unsuccessful in this appeal.
policy_considerations: The decision reflects a policy of maintaining the proper judicial hierarchy, where the High Court is the appropriate forum for the initial, detailed examination of complex issues. Remanding the case ensures that parties have the benefit of a full consideration at the High Court level before any potential review by the Supreme Court, thereby ensuring a more thorough and structured judicial process.
